item.title: The Heavy Heart of ‘Finally’ 60: Why It’s Okay to Grieve the Life You Expected
item.description: Many women feel a quiet kind of grief after turning 60. It’s not always about losing someone, a job, or a big event. Often, it comes from missing the life once pictured. In a world of curated social media feeds, it’s easy to feel like the only one mourning a "perfect" future that didn't arrive...

item.title: A Walking Oxymoron in Nine Small Stories
item.description: The word oxymoron comes from two Greek roots: oxys, meaning sharp or keen, and mōros, meaning dull or foolish. Put together, the word itself is a contradiction – sharp-dull – making oxymoron an oxymoron. It first appeared in English in the 1650s, which means for centuries we have delighted in pairing opposites and called it clever...
